We are pivoting the product. Offer Guard (checking ad promises) is dropped: our teammate showed it is not a proven problem in our agency and does not showcase Meta's models. The new product is **one creative → every placement size**, built on Meta's models. Working name: **AdFit** (a string in one place — `src/shared/brand.ts` — so it can be renamed later). Follow AGENTS.md. Live Model API calls allowed (Muse Image is $0.01/image; keep a session under ~$3). Never call the Graph API with --execute. Do not commit or push. Everything bilingual (English default, Hebrew toggle, RTL), as before.

## Why (keep this as the product story in README)
Our studio adapts every approved creative to 6–8 placement sizes by hand, every day, for 100+ brands. Generic AI resizers redraw the product, break Hebrew lettering and ignore the brand's own layout rules for each size. AdFit adapts with Meta's models and is trustworthy: brand templates per size, protected product/logo pixels with proof, and a model QA check on every output.

## What to reuse vs. remove
Reuse, don't rewrite: the Model API client, Spark extraction (structured output + pixel coords), SAM 3.1 masks + parser, Chromium text renderer with bundled Noto fonts, Sharp compositing, pixel proof + digest, SQLite store, trace collector, the Hono server (base path, media-by-id, SSE jobs, kill switch, queue, per-IP limit, daily cap, CSP, upload validation) and the web UI shell (header, EN/עב toggle, RTL, trace drawer, styles).
Remove from the product (git history keeps it): the Offer Guard UI screens, verdict/sweep/campaign/landing-page code and their fixtures/tests, unless a module is reused above. The repo must read as one coherent product. Keep docs/build/ as is (it is the honest build history; I will add the pivot row myself).

## Verified facts (tested today, don't re-research)
- `POST https://api.meta.ai/v1/images/edits`, JSON body: `{model:"muse-image-1.0", prompt, size:"WxH", images:[{image_url:"data:image/png;base64,..."}], output_format:"png", reasoning_strength:"low"|"high"}`. Up to 10 input images (multi-image composition works — pass the source and a template as references). `size` sets the **aspect ratio only**: 1080x1920 came back 1152x2048, 1080x1350 came back 1408x1760 → always resize/crop to the exact preset in code and verify. `mask`, `enable_web_search`, `enable_image_search` → 400 on edits. ~16–18 s per image, $0.01.
- Quality seen on the GALI fixture (`fixtures/ads/ad-01-clean.png`): a "recompose for 9:16, keep bottle/logo/offer panel and Hebrew text exactly" prompt produced correct Hebrew and a good layout, but the bottle is redrawn (slightly different proportions). A "remove bottle/logo/text/panel, output only the clean extended background" prompt produced a clean plate; compositing the original bottle (SAM mask) + logo + original panel pixels onto it looked right.

## 1. Sizes (presets in one table, user picks any subset)
Instagram feed 1080×1080 and 1080×1350 · Stories/Reels 1080×1920 · Facebook feed 1200×1200 · Facebook link 1200×628 · LinkedIn 1200×627 · YouTube 1280×720 · TikTok 1080×1920. Each preset has a safe area (e.g. top/bottom 14% kept clear on 9:16 for UI overlays).

## 2. Brands and templates (the key feature)
A **brand** has a name, colors, fonts (optional), a logo file, and **templates**. A template is a past finished creative of that brand in a given size, uploaded by the user — it teaches the brand's layout for that size. The user can upload several templates and assign a **different template per size** (or one default template for all sizes).
- On upload, **Spark reads the template** into a stored layout spec (JSON schema, pixel coords normalized to 0–1): logo box + corner, headline zone, sub-text zone, offer/CTA panel zone (with color/shape), product zone, frame elements (bands, tabs, corner shapes with color and edge), background style, text alignment and direction. **SAM** gives exact masks for logo and frame elements so they can be reused as pixels. The user sees the parsed template drawn as labeled boxes over the image and can nudge a box or reject a template (simple drag on the overlay is enough; no full editor).
- Optional **frame overlay**: a transparent PNG per size (brand frame/band) placed exactly by code, last.
- Brand auto-match: when a source creative is uploaded, Spark compares it to the stored brands (logo + colors) and proposes one; the user can override. No real client brand data may enter the repo: demo brands are synthetic only.

## 3. Generation pipeline (per source × per size)
1. **Analyze source** (Spark, once per source): elements with boxes — product(s), logo, headline (verbatim text), sub-text, offer/CTA panel, background type, language/direction. SAM masks for product + logo (union of phrase + box prompt from Spark's box, as in the repair pipeline).
2. **Plan layout** per size: from the brand template for that size if any (zones), else default rules (logo top corner by direction, product centered within the safe area, panel bottom). Plan is data, shown in the trace.
3. **Two modes** (user picks; default Protected):
   - **Fast**: Muse Image edit with [source, template-for-size if any] and a prompt built from the analysis + plan ("follow the layout of the second image", exact verbatim texts listed). Then exact-size resize/crop.
   - **Protected**: Muse Image generates a **background plate only** for the target ratio (style from source + template). Code then places the original product and logo as SAM-cut pixels (scaling allowed, never redrawn; scale factor recorded), places text: opaque panels are copied as pixel blocks, free text on the background is re-rendered by Chromium with the verbatim text (direction + font weight/color approximated from the source), and applies the frame overlay. Pixel proof per output: for each protected element, the pasted pixels equal the source pixels after the recorded transform (0 differing pixels), plus digest. Soft 1–2 px edge feather is allowed only outside the mask core — say so in the proof.
4. **QA by Spark** on every output (fresh call): reads the output and compares to the source analysis — every verbatim text present and exact, logo present and not cropped, product present and not cropped, nothing important inside the unsafe area, no invented text. Result PASS/FAIL with reasons. On FAIL: one automatic retry with the reasons added to the prompt, then mark "needs review". QA results and retries appear in the trace.
5. Concurrency: sizes of one job run 2 at a time; one job at a time globally (existing queue).

## 4. UI (same visual language as now; clean, few words, big previews)
- **Home**: upload one or more creatives (drag-drop), pick brand (auto-proposed), pick sizes (chips, with "all Meta placements" shortcut), mode (Protected / Fast), Generate. Results grid fills in live per size (SSE): image, size label, QA badge (✓ checked by Spark / ⚠ needs review), mode badge, regenerate (per size), download PNG; "Download all (ZIP)" with a manifest.
- **Detail per output**: before/after side by side at true aspect; overlay toggle (SAM masks of protected elements, template zones); proof numbers for Protected ("0 px changed in product / logo"), QA verdict with the texts Spark read back; trace drawer (model ids, durations, retries).
- **Brands**: list brands, create brand, upload logo + templates, assign template per size, see the parsed layout overlay, delete.
- **About**: how it works in 5 steps with the Meta model at each step; honest limits.
- Saved demo: a "Try the demo brand" path that shows a finished GALI job (cached, labeled with time) so judges see results instantly, plus a "Run it live" button.

## 5. Synthetic demo fixtures (no real brands)
- Brand **GALI** (existing fictional bottle brand): render templates for 1:1, 4:5, 9:16, 1.91:1 with `scripts/render-fixtures.ts`-style HTML (distinct per size: e.g. 9:16 has a teal bottom band with the logo inside, 1.91:1 puts product left and text right) + a logo PNG + one frame overlay. Source creatives: the existing `ad-01-clean.png` (he) and `ad-01-clean-en.png`.
- A second fictional brand with a **photographic** source, generated once with Muse Image (`/v1/images/generations`, store the output as a fixture, label it AI-generated synthetic in fixtures README) — e.g. a coffee brand "NOA" with a Hebrew headline on a photo — to show the pipeline on a harder, non-flat image. Give it templates for 2 sizes.
- `tests/fixtures/` expectations: which texts must survive per fixture (local only, never sent to a model).

## 6. Limits and safety (keep the existing ones)
Kill switch, one heavy job at a time + queue ≤3, 3 live jobs/IP/hour, daily cap now counts model calls **and** Muse Image images (`ADFIT_DAILY_IMAGES`, default 200). Uploads: JPEG/PNG/WebP by content, ≤10 MB, ≤24 MP, re-encoded (metadata stripped), deleted after 24 h; templates and brands created by visitors expire after 24 h too (demo brands are permanent fixtures). Max 8 sizes × 3 sources per job. Rename env vars to `ADFIT_*` and keep `.env.example` in sync (no secrets there).
